extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent agents/attorneys, and national/regional patent offices (receiving, searching, designated and elected offices)
extracted.subtask_description: Requirements, procedural steps, and substantive standards for filing and processing an international patent application under the Patent Cooperation Treaty (PCT), including filing content, search, publication, amendments, national-phase obligations, and remedies. Intended to guide applicants and offices in preparing, examining, searching, and communicating PCT applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required contents of the international application
rubrics_metrics.description: An international application shall contain a request, a description, one or more claims, one or more drawings (where required), and an abstract (Art.3(2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These elements are specified by the Treaty and Regulations and are prerequisites for processing and for being accorded an international filing date. Missing required parts may trigger invitations to correct or lead to the application being considered withdrawn.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract purpose limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: The abstract merely serves the purpose of technical information and cannot be taken into account for any other purpose, particularly not for interpreting the scope of protection sought (Art.3(3)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abstracts should summarize technical disclosure only; they must not be used as claim construction or affect legal scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prescribed language requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The international application shall be in a prescribed language (Art.3(4)(i)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Language requirements are set by the Regulations and affect whether an international filing date is accorded; translations may be required later for designated/elected Offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physical requirements of the application
rubrics_metrics.description: The international application must comply with the prescribed physical requirements (Art.3(4)(ii)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Physical requirements (paper size, margins, numbering, sequence listing formats, electronic formats, etc.) are set in the Regulations; failure to comply may be a defect inviting correction or may cause withdrawal if not corrected in time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity of invention requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The international application must comply with the prescribed requirement of unity of invention (Art.3(4)(iii)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the International Searching Authority (ISA) considers there is lack of unity it may invite payment of additional search fees and will search the 'main invention' first; national Offices may treat unsearched parts as withdrawn unless additional fees are paid. Rules and national law govern handling and protests (Art.17(3)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment of prescribed fees
rubrics_metrics.description: The international application shall be subject to the payment of the prescribed fees (Art.3(4)(iv)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Payment of filing, search, handling, designation, and national fees is mandatory; unpaid fees within prescribed time limits can lead to the application or particular designations being considered withdrawn (Art.14(3)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents of the Request (form)
rubrics_metrics.description: The request must contain a petition that the application be processed under the Treaty; designation of Contracting State(s) (and indication if regional patent sought); prescribed data concerning the applicant and agent (if any); title of the invention; and prescribed data concerning the inventor where required (Art.4(1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designations are subject to fees; where national law allows inventor data later, furnishing may be delayed as permitted. The request's content affects filing date and entitlement in designated states.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation fee and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Every designation shall be subject to payment of the prescribed fee within the prescribed time limit (Art.4(2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to pay designation fees on time can cause designations to be considered withdrawn for specific States; national-phase rules (e.g., 30-month rule) and Regulations set exact deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description (sufficiency / enablement)
rubrics_metrics.description: The description shall disclose the invention in a manner sufficiently clear and complete for the invention to be carried out by a person skilled in the art (Art.5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an enablement requirement: the description must support the claims and provide technical teaching enabling practice of the invention without undue experimentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims: definition, clarity, and support
rubrics_metrics.description: The claim or claims shall define the matter for which protection is sought. Claims shall be clear and concise and shall be fully supported by the description (Art.6).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims draftsmanship must ensure clarity, concision, and basis in the description; lack of support or unclear claims can trigger objections, affect search/examination, and limit enforceable scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings: required when necessary
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings shall be required when necessary for the understanding of the invention. Where not necessary, drawings may be included by the applicant and a designated Office may require such drawings to be filed within a prescribed time (Art.7(1)-(2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the international application references drawings not included, the applicant may supply them within a time limit; otherwise references are considered non-existent (Art.14(2)). Designated Offices can demand illustrative drawings even if not essential initially.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant eligibility by residence or nationality
rubrics_metrics.description: Any resident or national of a Contracting State may file an international application. The Assembly may permit residents/nationals of Paris Convention countries that are not party to the PCT to file (Art.9).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules in the Regulations define residence/nationality concepts in multi-applicant cases; eligibility affects which Receiving Office may accept the filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claiming priority
rubrics_metrics.description: The international application may contain a declaration claiming the priority of one or more earlier applications filed in or for any country party to the Paris Convention; conditions and effects of priority are governed by the Paris Convention and national law where specified (Art.8(1)-(2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Priority claims must follow Regulations (formalities, timing); for certain national law aspects (e.g., effect of priority in a designated State) national law may govern; priority documents/translations and time limits are prescribed by Rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing with the prescribed Receiving Office
rubrics_metrics.description: The international application shall be filed with the prescribed receiving Office, which will check and process it as provided in the Treaty and Regulations (Art.10).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choice of Receiving Office depends on applicant eligibility and national/regional rules; the Receiving Office performs initial formality checks and determines the international filing date subject to compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for accorded international filing date
rubrics_metrics.description: The receiving Office shall accord as the international filing date the date of receipt provided that, at time of receipt, the applicant does not obviously lack the right to file there, the application is in the prescribed language, and the application contains at least: an indication it is intended as an international application; designation of at least one Contracting State; name of the applicant; a part appearing to be a description; and a part appearing to be a claim or claims (Art.11(1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These minimal elements determine whether the filing date is credited; if elements are missing the RO will invite correction per Regulations and a corrected date may be accorded if corrected in time (Art.11(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of defects and effect on filing date
rubrics_metrics.description: If the receiving Office finds missing/defective required elements it shall invite the applicant to file the required correction; if the applicant complies within Regulations, the receiving Office shall accord as the international filing date the date of receipt of the required correction (Art.11(2); Art.14(1)(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invitations to correct are governed by prescribed time limits; failure to correct within time may lead to the application being considered withdrawn.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of omitted or missing drawings referenced
rubrics_metrics.description: If the international application refers to drawings which are not included, the receiving Office shall notify the applicant and he may furnish them within the prescribed time limit; if not furnished references to such drawings are considered non-existent (Art.14(2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should supply missing drawings promptly to avoid loss of disclosure that may be relied on in search and national phases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal consequences for unpaid fees or missing formalities
rubrics_metrics.description: If fees prescribed under Art.3(4)(iv) or Art.4(2) are not paid within prescribed time limits the international application shall be considered withdrawn; partial payment can cause some designations to be considered withdrawn (Art.14(3)). Also if requirements listed for filing date were not complied with at that date, the application shall be considered withdrawn (Art.14(4)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict compliance with fee payments and formalities is required; some situations allow restoration or review per national law or Article 48 provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory international search and its objective
rubrics_metrics.description: Each international application shall be the subject of an international search whose objective is to discover relevant prior art (Art.15(1)-(2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The ISR is a key international document informing applicant and designated Offices of prior art; ISRs are produced by appointed International Searching Authorities under Rules and Agreements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basis and scope of the international search
rubrics_metrics.description: International search shall be made on the basis of the claims, with due regard to the description and the drawings (Art.15(3)); the ISA shall endeavor to discover as much relevant prior art as its facilities permit and shall consult documentation specified in the Regulations (Art.15(4)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claim clarity and support affect search scope; the ISA's documentation holdings and capacities limit the extent of prior art retrieved; applicants may request international-type searches for certain national filings where permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appointment and minimum requirements for International Searching Authorities (ISA)
rubrics_metrics.description: ISAs shall be appointed by the Assembly; any national Office or intergovernmental organization satisfying minimum requirements (particularly manpower and documentation) may be appointed; appointment is conditional on consent and an agreement with the International Bureau (Art.16(3)(a)-(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appointment criteria ensure quality and uniformity of ISRs; Regulations set specific minimum standards that must be maintained for continued appointment.

rubrics_metrics.name: ISA procedure: refusal to search where meaningful search cannot be carried out
rubrics_metrics.description: If the ISA considers the subject matter is not required to be searched or that the description, claims, or drawings fail to comply with requirements to such an extent that a meaningful search could not be carried out, the ISA shall declare that no international search report will be established (Art.17(2)(a)). If only certain claims are affected, the ISA will indicate which claims were not searched (Art.17(2)(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must ensure clarity and formal compliance; a declaration of no ISR affects communication to DOs and may trigger other procedural consequences and time limits under the Regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity objections, additional search fees, and national consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: If the ISA considers the application lacks unity of invention it shall invite payment of additional fees; the ISA will establish the ISR for the 'main invention' and for other inventions if additional fees are paid; national law may treat unsearched parts as withdrawn with respect to effects in that State unless a special fee is paid (Art.17(3)(a)-(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants can respond to unity objections by paying additional fees; protests and refunds may be available under Rules; national-phase consequences depend on each designated State's law.

rubrics_metrics.name: International Search Report (ISR): timing and transmission
rubrics_metrics.description: The ISR shall be established within the prescribed time limit and in the prescribed form and shall be transmitted by the ISA to the applicant and the International Bureau as soon as established (Art.18(1)-(2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely ISR issuance triggers applicant rights to amend claims before the IB and starts publication and communication processes; prescribed time limits are in the Regulations and Rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability and translation of cited documents
rubrics_metrics.description: At the request of the designated Office or the applicant, the ISA shall send copies of the documents cited in the ISR as provided in the Regulations; the ISR or declaration and its translations shall be prepared by or under responsibility of the International Bureau (Art.18(3); Art.19(3)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Access to cited prior art documents supports national examination and applicant responses; translations and transmittal procedures and time limits are governed by the Regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment of claims before the International Bureau
rubrics_metrics.description: After receiving the ISR the applicant is entitled to one opportunity to amend the claims by filing amendments with the International Bureau within the prescribed time limit and may file a brief statement explaining amendments and impacts; amendments shall not go beyond the disclosure in the international application as filed (Art.21(1)-(2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments must remain within original disclosure (no added matter) for PCT purposes; some designated States' national law may permit broader amendments with differing effects in those States (Art.21(3)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Communication to designated Offices (content and translations)
rubrics_metrics.description: The international application together with the ISR (or declaration) shall be communicated to each designated Office per the Regulations and shall include prescribed translations; if claims were amended under Art.19(1), the communication shall contain full texts of claims both as filed and as amended, specify amendments, and include the Art.19(1) statement if any (Art.20(1)-(2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DOs receive both original and ISR to conduct national processing; accurate translations and clear indication of amended claims are crucial for consistent national examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: International publication timing and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: International publication of the international application shall be effected promptly after 18 months from the priority date (subject to exceptions); applicant may request earlier publication; the ISR or declaration shall also be published as prescribed; the IB may omit passages contrary to morality or public order or disparaging statements, indicating omissions and providing copies on request (Art.21(2)-(6)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication places the disclosure in the public domain and affects prior art status; applicants can request early publication and should consider content that may be omitted by IB for morality/disparagement reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: National-phase entry obligations (copy, translation, national fee and 30-month time limit)
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant shall furnish a copy of the international application and a translation (as prescribed), and pay the national fee (if any) to each designated Office not later than the expiration of 30 months from the priority date (Art.22(1); editor's note: 30-month rule in force from April 1, 2002, with exceptions where Offices notified incompatibility).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deadlines vary by designated State and some States allow later times or different rules; failure to perform acts within the time limit can lead to loss of effect in that State (Art.24). Where ISA made a declaration of no ISR, the same time limit applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delaying national procedure and applicant-requested early processing
rubrics_metrics.description: No designated Office shall process or examine the international application prior to the expiration of the applicable time limit under Art.22, but a designated Office may process or examine earlier on the express request of the applicant (Art.23(1)-(2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants who want earlier national processing can request it; otherwise national Offices typically wait until national-phase entry time limits expire.

rubrics_metrics.name: Possible loss of effect in designated States
rubrics_metrics.description: The effect of the international application as a regular national filing shall cease in any designated State with the same consequences as withdrawal if: the applicant withdraws the international application or the designation; the international application is considered withdrawn under specified Articles; or the applicant fails to perform acts referred to in Art.22 within the applicable time limit (Art.24(1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designations can be lost by applicant action or procedural failures; some designated Offices may nevertheless maintain effect in that State; applicants must monitor deadlines and payments carefully.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review by designated Offices of Receiving Office / International Bureau adverse determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the RO refused to accord an international filing date or declared the application considered withdrawn (or IB made a finding under Art.12(3)), the IB shall, at applicant request, send copies of any document to designated Offices; designated Offices shall decide whether the refusal/declaration/finding was justified and, if it resulted from an RO/IB error or omission, may treat the application as if such error had not occurred provided national fee and translation were furnished in time (Art.25(1)-(2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DO review can remediate certain RO/IB errors affecting national effects; applicants must request transmittal within prescribed time limits and comply with DO's requirements (fees/translations) to benefit from a favorable DO review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity to correct before designated Offices (no rejection without chance to correct)
rubrics_metrics.description: No designated Office shall reject an international application on the grounds of non-compliance with Treaty/Regulations requirements without first giving the applicant the opportunity to correct the application to the extent and according to the procedure provided by the national law for comparable national applications (Art.26).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This affords applicants procedural fairness in national phase; the extent and form of correction follow national law procedures and time limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitation on national requirements (form and content)
rubrics_metrics.description: No national law shall require compliance with form or content requirements different from or additional to those provided in this Treaty and the Regulations; however, national law may require certain documents once processing in the designated Office has started (e.g., name of officer for legal entity, proof documents), and may reject an application if applicant not qualified under national law to file a national application (Art.27(1)-(3)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PCT centralizes formal requirements; nevertheless national-phase formalities (proofs, signatures, representative qualifications) and substantive national law (e.g., who may be applicant) still apply. Where national law is more favorable to applicants, those national requirements may be applied instead of PCT ones (Art.27(4)).
